source "https://rubygems.org"
git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

ruby "3.3.6"

# Bundle edge Rails instead: gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
gem "rails", "7.0.8.7"
gem "concurrent-ruby", "1.3.4"

# The original asset pipeline for Rails [https://github.com/rails/sprockets-rails]
gem "sprockets-rails"

# Use postgresql as the database for Active Record
gem "pg", "1.6.0"

# Use the Puma web server [https://github.com/puma/puma]
gem "puma", "~> 5.0"

# Use JavaScript with ESM import maps [https://github.com/rails/importmap-rails]
gem "importmap-rails"

# Hotwire's SPA-like page accelerator [https://turbo.hotwired.dev]
gem "turbo-rails"

# Hotwire's modest JavaScript framework [https://stimulus.hotwired.dev]
gem "stimulus-rails"

# Build JSON APIs with ease [https://github.com/rails/jbuilder]
gem "jbuilder"

# Paginate the note list [https://github.com/ddnexus/pagy]
gem "pagy", "8.6.3"

# Run Active Job on Redis through Sidekiq [https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq]
gem "sidekiq", "6.5.12"
gem "redis", "4.8.1"

# Request citation metadata over HTTP [https://github.com/lostisland/faraday]
gem "faraday", "1.10.4"

# Use Kredis to get higher-level data types in Redis [https://github.com/rails/kredis]
# gem "kredis"

# Use Active Model has_secure_password [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_model_basics.html#securepassword]
gem "bcrypt", "~> 3.1.7"

# Windows does not include zoneinfo files, so bundle the tzinfo-data gem
gem "tzinfo-data", platforms: %i[ mingw mswin x64_mingw jruby ]

# Reduces boot times through caching; required in config/boot.rb
gem "bootsnap", require: false

# Use Sass to process CSS
# gem "sassc-rails"

# Use Active Storage variants [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_storage_overview.html#transforming-images]
# gem "image_processing", "~> 1.2"

group :development, :test do
  # See https://guides.rubyonrails.org/debugging_rails_applications.html#debugging-with-the-debug-gem
  gem "debug", platforms: %i[ mri mingw x64_mingw ]
end

group :development do
  # Use console on exceptions pages [https://github.com/rails/web-console]
  gem "web-console"

  # Add speed badges [https://github.com/MiniProfiler/rack-mini-profiler]
  # gem "rack-mini-profiler"

  # Speed up commands on slow machines / big apps [https://github.com/rails/spring]
  # gem "spring"
end

group :test do
  # Use system testing [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/testing.html#system-testing]
  gem "capybara"
  gem "selenium-webdriver"

  # Rails 7.0's test runner is incompatible with Minitest 6
  gem "minitest", "~> 5.25"
end

     3	# config/secrets.yml, which reads them from the environment.
     4	class Citation::Provider
     5	  # The provider answered, but cannot supply metadata for this DOI.
     6	  class Error < StandardError; end
     7	
     8	  # The provider cannot answer now. Asking again later may succeed.
     9	  class Unavailable < StandardError; end
    10	
    11	  Metadata = Struct.new(:title, :source_url)
    12	
    13	  def initialize(settings = Rails.application.secrets.citation_provider.to_h)
    14	    @url, @user, @password = settings.values_at(:url, :user, :password)
    15	  end
    16	
    17	  def lookup(doi)
    18	    raise Error, "No citation provider is configured" if @url.blank?
    19	
    20	    response = connection.get("works", doi: doi)
    21	
    22	    case response.status
    23	    when 200 then metadata_from(response.body)
    24	    when 401, 403 then raise Error, "The provider rejected the configured credentials (HTTP #{response.status})"
    25	    when 404 then raise Error, "The provider has no record of this DOI"
    26	    when 429, 500..599 then raise Unavailable, "The provider is unavailable (HTTP #{response.status})"
    27	    else raise Error, "The provider gave an unexpected response (HTTP #{response.status})"
    28	    end
    29	  rescue Faraday::ConnectionFailed, Faraday::TimeoutError => error
    30	    raise Unavailable, "The provider could not be reached (#{error.message})"
    31	  end
    32	
    33	  private
    34	    # Retries a GET once on 503 before reporting the provider unavailable.
    35	    def connection
    36	      Faraday.new(url: @url, request: { open_timeout: 2, timeout: 5 }) do |faraday|
    37	        faraday.request :retry, max: 1, retry_statuses: [503]
    38	        faraday.request :basic_auth, @user, @password
    39	      end
    40	    end
    41	
    42	    def metadata_from(body)
    43	      attributes = JSON.parse(body)
    44	      title, source_url = attributes["title"], attributes["url"] if attributes.is_a?(Hash)
    45	
    46	      if title.is_a?(String) && title.present? && web_url?(source_url)
    47	        Metadata.new(title.strip, source_url)
    48	      else
    49	        raise Error, "The provider's response did not include a title and web address"
    50	      end
    51	    rescue JSON::ParserError
    52	      raise Error, "The provider's response was not valid JSON"
    53	    end
    54	
    55	    def web_url?(url)
    56	      uri = URI.parse(url.to_s)
    57	      uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present?
    58	    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
    59	      false
    60	    end
    61	end

41	    41	  from the name on creation and is read-only afterward (`attr_readonly`). The
42	    42	  settings form resubmits it unchanged. The export heading is stored in the

45	    45	  reads the upload and renders a preview without saving. The preview page sends

47	    47	  validates it again rather than trusting the preview. `Import#apply` saves the

50	    50	  each imported note's title and DOI. Submitting the same preview twice creates

58	    58	  shared by every reader who cites it. A DOI is stored as given apart from
59	    59	  surrounding whitespace, so case variants are different citations. Rows in one
60	    60	  import share a new citation. Two simultaneous imports that introduce the same
61	    61	  new DOI can conflict; the losing request fails with a server error and saves
62	    62	  nothing. A reader's annotation and optional reminder epoch belong to the note,
63	    63	  not the citation. Annotations are plain text in both the preview and note page;
64	    64	  line breaks are preserved on the note page, but markup is displayed literally.
65	    65	  Applying an import does not schedule its reminders; the reader schedules each
66	    66	  one from its note.
67	    67	- A reader can also enter a DOI on the note form (`Note#doi=`), which cites the
68	    68	  shared citation with that exact, trimmed DOI or creates it.
69	    69	- A reader requests metadata for the citation on one of their notes with
70	    70	  `CitationEnrichmentsController#create`, nested under the note. It resolves the
71	    71	  note through `current_user.notes`, so another reader's note, or a note without
72	    72	  a DOI, is a 404. `Citation#request_enrichment` marks the citation pending and
73	    73	  queues `CitationEnrichmentJob`, unless a request is already pending. The job
74	    74	  calls `Citation#enrich`, which stores the provider's title and source URL and
75	    75	  marks the citation completed, or records a failure message. Metadata and
76	    76	  status belong to the shared citation, so every note citing the DOI shows them.
77	    77	  The note page shows the state; it does not update itself while pending.
78	    78	- `Citation::Provider` is the HTTP client for the metadata provider. It reads
79	    79	  its URL and basic-auth credentials from [config/secrets.yml](config/secrets.yml)

81	    81	  Faraday retries a GET once on 503. A 401, 403, or 404, or a response without a
82	    82	  title and an http(s) URL, fails the enrichment at once. A 429 or 5xx, timeout,

85	    85	  records the failure instead of passing the error to Sidekiq's own retries. A
86	    86	  persistently unavailable provider therefore receives at most six requests per
87	    87	  enrichment request. A job that fails for another reason uses Sidekiq's retries

90	    90	  for the provider, used for development and demonstrations. No real provider or

93	    93	  (`ExportsController`, nested under the notebook). `Notebook#request_export`

97	    97	  export is removed and the request fails. Each request creates a new export.
98	    98	- `Export#generate`, run by the worker, marks the export working with the
99	    99	  notebook's note count, then writes the notes oldest first (creation time, then
100	   100	  ID). The file starts with the notebook's export heading, or its name when none
101	   101	  is set. Each note is a second-level heading with its title on one line,
102	   102	  followed by its body as Action Text plain text. Markdown characters are not
103	   103	  escaped. Progress is saved after each note. A retried job starts again from

105	   105	  the export shows as working and the reader can cancel it.
106	   106	- Cancelling (`ExportCancellationsController`) sets a queued or working export's
107	   107	  persisted status to cancelled under its row lock. The worker checks that status
108	   108	  before each note and before completing, then stops and keeps no file. Completed
109	   109	  and cancelled exports cannot be cancelled.

111	   111	  export completed, so a completed export always has a file. It can be downloaded
112	   112	  for 24 hours (`Export::AVAILABLE_FOR`). `ExportDownloadsController` resolves the
113	   113	  export through the reader's notebook, so another reader's export is a 404, and
114	   114	  checks `Export#downloadable?` on every request before any conditional response.
115	   115	  An expired, cancelled, or unfinished export redirects to the exports page. The
116	   116	  file is sent by the application, never by an Active Storage URL, with an ETag
117	   117	  and Last-Modified from the stored file and `private, must-revalidate`.
118	   118	  A failed upload can leave an unattached blob row without a stored file. Nothing
119	   119	  cleans up those rows, and each failed retry can leave another one.
120	   120	- The exports page caches each completed export's availability indicator as a

125	   125	  notebook and linked from the notebooks list) shows how many of its notes were

127	   127	  notebook through `current_user.notebooks`, so another reader's notebook is a
128	   128	  404. `Notebook#daily_note_counts` groups the notes by `DATE(created_at)` in
129	   129	  PostgreSQL and reads the rows with a raw `select_rows`, which returns each date
130	   130	  as ISO 8601 text; the method parses it with `Date.iso8601`. Every status counts,
131	   131	  and dates without notes are omitted. The report is derived from the notes that

140	   140	  (`User#local_time`), or, with none, uses the stored time. `Note#schedule_reminder`

147	   147	  reminder. Earlier jobs stay in Sidekiq's schedule, but send nothing: when a job

154	   154	  that time as `reminder_at.to_time + 86_400`, which keeps the reminder's UTC
155	   155	  offset. Across a daylight saving change the preview shows the right instant,

158	   158	  (`DigestsController`). `User#request_digest` reserves the reader's ID in a

161	   161	  the reader, the request time in the reader's zone, and the share of their notes
162	   162	  that are ready, as a `BigDecimal`. A reader whose ID is already in the day's set

173	   173	  by it. The content day matches the reservation's day, even near local midnight.

175	   175	  in a second digest for that UTC day.

217	   217	## Prefer Rails objects with clear responsibilities
218	   218	
219	   219	Use the framework's ordinary directories and interfaces:
220	   220	
221	   221	| Responsibility | Home |
222	   222	| --- | --- |
223	   223	| HTTP verbs, paths, and resource nesting | `config/routes.rb` |
224	   224	| Parameter selection, authorized lookup, response negotiation | `app/controllers/` |
225	   225	| Persistent state and domain operations | `app/models/` |
226	   226	| A cohesive capability of one model | A namespace beneath `app/models/` |
227	   227	| Behavior genuinely shared across models | `app/models/concerns/` |
228	   228	| HTML, Turbo stream, and JSON representations | `app/views/` |
229	   229	| Presentation helpers | `app/helpers/` |
230	   230	| Browser interaction around rendered HTML | `app/javascript/controllers/` |
231	   231	| Background execution and retry boundary | `app/jobs/` |
232	   232	| Mail composition | `app/mailers/` and its views |
233	   233	
234	   234	A controller can call Active Record directly for a simple save. A multi-step
235	   235	domain transition belongs behind a meaningful model method, not a sequence of
236	   236	unrelated updates in the controller. Use a plain Ruby object or Active Model when
237	   237	an operation needs its own object but no database table. Do not introduce a
238	   238	mandatory service, repository, presenter, or command layer between every pair of
239	   239	Rails objects.
240	   240	
241	   241	Fizzy models closing a card as a singular closure resource. Its controller calls
242	   242	`Card#close`, and `Card::Closeable` owns the association, predicates, and transaction.
243	   243	The [closure sources](docs/references/fizzy.md#card-closure) illustrate a resource
244	   244	boundary and a domain method, not a requirement to add cards to Margin Notes.
245	   245	
246	   246	## Model resources, not collections of verbs
247	   247	
248	   248	Use the conventional REST actions, including `new` and `edit` for HTML forms.
249	   249	When a new operation does not fit an existing resource, look for the resource it
250	   250	creates, updates, or removes before adding a custom action. Keep nesting shallow
251	   251	enough that the parent conveys ownership rather than reproducing the whole schema.
252	   252	
253	   253	Use route helpers in views and responses. Controllers choose the representation.
254	   254	Models do not construct controller responses or reach into request parameters.
255	   255	
256	   256	## Keep data ownership and effects explicit
257	   257	
258	   258	- PostgreSQL owns durable application facts. Derive a value from those facts
259	   259	  unless storing it solves a demonstrated query, history, or concurrency need.
260	   260	- Put invariants used outside HTTP in the domain model. Add database constraints
261	   261	  when integrity must also hold across concurrent requests and non-model writes.
262	   262	- Keep related database writes in one transaction. Do not assume it can undo a
263	   263	  remote request, an email, or a job already sent to another system.
264	   264	- Jobs should delegate to domain behavior and carry the identifiers or context
265	   265	  they need. Decide retries, duplicate delivery, and transaction timing when a
266	   266	  real background feature is introduced, rather than adding a queue preemptively.
267	   267	- Keep network clients at visible boundaries. Preserve failure information and
268	   268	  distinguish a legitimate empty response from a failed operation.
269	   269	
270	   270	Fizzy's [comment example](docs/references/fizzy.md#comments) enforces comment
271	   271	eligibility in both the model and the controller. Callers outside HTTP must obey
272	   272	the same rule.
273	   273	
274	   274	## Authorization is not presentation
275	   275	
276	   276	Define ownership and the authorized lookup scope together. Resolve records
277	   277	through the signed-in reader: `current_user.notebooks` and `current_user.notes`.
278	   278	Direct lookups outside that scope raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, which is
279	   279	a 404 in production. A submitted `notebook_id` is resolved through
280	   280	`current_user.notebooks.find_by`, never assigned directly. A missing or foreign
281	   281	notebook fails validation and renders the form with 422, without saving the note.
282	   282	Resolve nested records through their authorized parent. Neither an unguessable ID
283	   283	nor a hidden or disabled button grants or checks permission.
284	   284	
285	   285	Keep actor-dependent decisions explicit in domain APIs and reusable rendering.
286	   286	If request-local state is introduced, set and reset it at the request boundary.
287	   287	Jobs, mailers, and tests must not rely on a previous request having populated it.
288	   288	Do not adopt a tenancy or identity scheme solely because a reference application
289	   289	uses one.
290	   290	
291	   291	## Render on the server, enhance in the browser
292	   292	
293	   293	Use HTML forms and links for their native semantics. Turbo handles navigation,
294	   294	frames, and targeted replacements. Stimulus supplies local interaction that HTML
295	   295	does not provide. Keep persistence and authorization on the server, not in a
296	   296	second client-side model of the domain.
297	   297	
298	   298	Partials take the resources and presentation inputs they need. A template may
299	   299	compose several resources. A reusable partial should not depend on a particular
300	   300	controller's incidental instance variables or on undeclared request context.
301	   301	See the [view guide](docs/guides/views.md) for HTML, accessibility, Turbo, and JSON.
302	   302	
303	   303	## Optimize the actual representation
304	   304	
305	   305	Start with correct queries and clear response contracts. Filter and order before
306	   306	pagination. Use a stable tie-breaker where page membership must be deterministic.
307	   307	Load the associations that the rendered representation uses rather than adding
308	   308	a universal preload list to every request.
309	   309	
310	   310	Define cache keys and invalidation rules before introducing caching. Include
311	   311	permissions, locale, and related-record changes when they affect the output, or
312	   312	keep those parts outside the shared fragment. The
313	   313	[board example](docs/references/fizzy.md#boards-and-caching) illustrates why a
314	   314	warm cache must be tested with another viewer, not just the same request twice.
315	   315	
316	   316	## Scope and reference boundaries
317	   317	
318	   318	The [public examples](docs/references/fizzy.md) are evidence for design ideas, not
319	   319	a compatible application template. Their Ruby, Rails, database adapters, asset
320	   320	pipeline, editors, and helper libraries differ from this repository. Use the
321	   321	locked local APIs, and introduce new infrastructure only for a requested feature.
322	   322	
323	   323	As features land, document their ownership and invariants here. Keep detailed
324	   324	layer practices in the [model](docs/guides/models.md),
325	   325	[controller](docs/guides/controllers.md), and [view](docs/guides/views.md) guides,
326	   326	and verification rules in [TESTING.md](TESTING.md).

329	     3	## Test the contract at its boundary
330	     4	
331	     5	Use Rails' Minitest integration with real application objects and the test
332	     6	PostgreSQL database. Exercise the route, controller, model, and rendering stack
333	     7	for HTTP behavior. When needed, substitute a controlled response at an external
334	     8	boundary. Do not stub the domain behavior under test.
335	     9	
336	    10	Choose the smallest boundary that can catch the likely mistake:
337	    11	
338	    12	| Contract | Test |
339	    13	| --- | --- |
340	    14	| A domain decision, transition, or query | `ActiveSupport::TestCase` in `test/models/` |
341	    15	| Routing, permissions, persistence, HTML, Turbo, or JSON | `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest` in `test/controllers/` |
342	    16	| A workflow across endpoints | An integration test in `test/integration/` |
343	    17	| Browser execution, focus, navigation, or JavaScript interaction | `ApplicationSystemTestCase` in `test/system/` |
344	    18	| Scheduling, delivery, and job-specific failure behavior | Rails job and mailer test helpers, usually in the request test that queues the job |
345	    19	
346	    20	Do not add a separate test for every method. Prefer assertions that would survive
347	    21	an internal refactor. A useful regression test fails for a plausible wrong
348	    22	implementation, not just a syntax error.

391	    65	## Make scenarios distinguish the right behavior
392	    66	
393	    67	- Name the domain fact or user outcome: a rejected edit leaves the body unchanged,
394	    68	  not merely that an update action runs.
395	    69	- Keep arrangement, action, and assertions recognizable. Share setup only for
396	    70	  facts every test in that group needs. Do not hide the decisive input in a helper.
397	    71	- Establish meaningful preconditions when the operation could otherwise be a
398	    72	  no-op. Reload records when checking what was persisted.
399	    73	- Use asymmetric values and contrasting records. A permission test needs another
400	    74	  user's record. A filter needs both an included and an excluded candidate.
401	    75	- Derive expected results independently. Do not call the production scope or
402	    76	  serializer to compute the value the same scope or serializer should return.
403	    77	- Assert order only where ordering is promised. For membership, include/exclude
404	    78	  assertions can express the rule better than an exact count of unrelated fixtures.
405	    79	  Assert total counts when pagination, duplicates, or filtering totals are contractual.

# frozen_string_literal: true

gem "sidekiq", ">= 4.1.0"
require "sidekiq"

module ActiveJob
  module QueueAdapters
    # = Sidekiq adapter for Active Job
    #
    # Simple, efficient background processing for Ruby. Sidekiq uses threads to
    # handle many jobs at the same time in the same process. It does not
    # require \Rails but will integrate tightly with it to make background
    # processing dead simple.
    #
    # Read more about Sidekiq {here}[http://sidekiq.org].
    #
    # To use Sidekiq set the queue_adapter config to +:sidekiq+.
    #
    #   Rails.application.config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq
    class SidekiqAdapter < AbstractAdapter
      def initialize(*) # :nodoc:
        @stopping = false

        Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end

        Sidekiq.configure_client do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end
      end

      def check_adapter
        ActiveJob.deprecator.warn <<~MSG.squish
          The built-in `sidekiq` adapter is deprecated and will be removed in Rails 8.2.
          Please upgrade `sidekiq` gem to version 7.3.3 or later to use the `sidekiq` gem's adapter.
        MSG
      end

      def enqueue(job) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name
        ).perform_async(job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_at(job, timestamp) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name,
        ).perform_at(timestamp, job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_all(jobs) # :nodoc:
        enqueued_count = 0
        jobs.group_by(&:class).each do |job_class, same_class_jobs|
          same_class_jobs.group_by(&:queue_name).each do |queue, same_class_and_queue_jobs|
            immediate_jobs, scheduled_jobs = same_class_and_queue_jobs.partition { |job| job.scheduled_at.nil? }

            if immediate_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "global_id/railtie"
require "active_job"

module ActiveJob
  # = Active Job Railtie
  class Railtie < Rails::Railtie # :nodoc:
    config.active_job = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
    config.active_job.custom_serializers = []
    config.active_job.log_query_tags_around_perform = true

    initializer "active_job.deprecator", before: :load_environment_config do |app|
      app.deprecators[:active_job] = ActiveJob.deprecator
    end

    initializer "active_job.logger" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) { self.logger = ::Rails.logger }
    end

    initializer "active_job.custom_serializers" do |app|
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        custom_serializers = app.config.active_job.custom_serializers
        ActiveJob::Serializers.add_serializers custom_serializers
      end
    end

    initializer "active_job.enqueue_after_transaction_commit" do |app|
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record) do
          ActiveJob::Base.include EnqueueAfterTransactionCommit
        end
      end
    end

    initializer "active_job.action_controller_parameters" do |app|
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_controller) do
          ActiveJob::Serializers.add_serializers ActiveJob::Serializers::ActionControllerParametersSerializer
        end
      end
    end

    initializer "active_job.set_configs" do |app|
      options = app.config.active_job
      options.queue_adapter ||= (Rails.env.test? ? :test : :async)

      config.after_initialize do
        options.each do |k, v|
          k = "#{k}="
          if ActiveJob.respond_to?(k)
            ActiveJob.send(k, v)
          end
        end
      end

      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        # Configs used in other initializers
        options = options.except(
          :log_query_tags_around_perform,
          :custom_serializers,
          # This config can't be applied globally, so we need to remove otherwise it will be applied to `ActiveJob::Base`.
          :enqueue_after_transaction_commit
        )

        options.each do |k, v|
          k = "#{k}="
          if ActiveJob.respond_to?(k)
            ActiveJob.send(k, v)
          elsif respond_to? k
            send(k, v)
          end
        end
      end

      ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_dispatch_integration_test) do
        include ActiveJob::TestHelper
      end
    end

    initializer "active_job.set_reloader_hook" do |app|
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        ActiveJob::Callbacks.singleton_class.set_callback(:execute, :around, prepend: true) do |_, inner|
          app.reloader.wrap do
            inner.call
          end
        end
      end
    end

  module Enqueuing
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    included do
      ##
      # :singleton-method:
      #
      # Defines if enqueueing this job from inside an Active Record transaction
      # automatically defers the enqueue to after the transaction commits.
      #
      # It can be set on a per job basis:
      #  - true forces the job to be deferred.
      #  - false forces the job to be queued immediately.
      class_attribute :enqueue_after_transaction_commit, instance_accessor: false, instance_predicate: false, default: false
    end

    # Includes the +perform_later+ method for job initialization.
    module ClassMethods
      # Push a job onto the queue. By default the arguments must be either String,
      # Integer, Float, NilClass, TrueClass, FalseClass, BigDecimal, Symbol, Date,
      # Time, DateTime, ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone, ActiveSupport::Duration,
      # Hash, ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess, Array, Range, or
      # GlobalID::Identification instances, although this can be extended by adding
      # custom serializers.
      #
      # Returns an instance of the job class queued with arguments available in
      # Job#arguments or +false+ if the enqueue did not succeed.
      #
      # After the attempted enqueue, the job will be yielded to an optional block.
      #
      # If Active Job is used conjointly with Active Record, and #perform_later is called
      # inside an Active Record transaction, then the enqueue is implicitly deferred to after
      # the transaction is committed, or dropped if it's rolled back. In such case #perform_later
      # will return the job instance like if it was successfully enqueued, but will still return
      # +false+ if a callback prevented the job from being enqueued.
      #
      # This behavior can be changed on a per job basis:
      #
      #  class NotificationJob < ApplicationJob
      #    self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = false
      #  end
      def perform_later(...)
        job = job_or_instantiate(...)
        enqueue_result = job.enqueue

        yield job if block_given?

        enqueue_result
      end

      private
        def job_or_instantiate(*args, &) # :doc:
          args.first.is_a?(self) ? args.first : new(*args)
        end
        ruby2_keywords(:job_or_instantiate)
    end

    # Enqueues the job to be performed by the queue adapter.
    #
    # ==== Options
    # * <tt>:wait</tt> - Enqueues the job with the specified delay
# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActiveJob
  module EnqueueAfterTransactionCommit # :nodoc:
    private
      def raw_enqueue
        if self.class.enqueue_after_transaction_commit
          self.successfully_enqueued = true
          ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do
            self.successfully_enqueued = false
            super
          end
          self
        else
          super
        end
      end
  end
end

*   Don't execute i18n watcher on boot. It shouldn't catch any file changes initially,
    and unnecessarily slows down boot of applications with lots of translations.

    *Gannon McGibbon*, *David Stosik*

*   Fix `ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess#stringify_keys` to stringify all keys not just symbols.

    Previously:

    ```ruby
    { 1 => 2 }.with_indifferent_access.stringify_keys[1] # => 2
    ```

    After this change:

    ```ruby
    { 1 => 2 }.with_indifferent_access.stringify_keys["1"] # => 2
    ```

    This change can be seen as a bug fix, but since it behaved like this for a very long time, we're deciding
    to not backport the fix and to make the change in a major release.

    *Jean Boussier*

      DEFAULT_OPTIONS = { escape: false }.freeze

      def dump(obj)
        @encoder.encode(obj)

      def load(json)
        ActiveSupport::JSON.decode(json, @options) unless json.blank?

# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActiveJob
  module Serializers
    class TimeWithZoneSerializer < ObjectSerializer # :nodoc:
      NANO_PRECISION = 9

      def serialize(time_with_zone)
        super(
          "value" => time_with_zone.iso8601(NANO_PRECISION),
          "time_zone" => time_with_zone.time_zone.tzinfo.name

        ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone
      end
    end
  end

      end
    end
  end

*   Do not trigger immediate loading of `ActiveJob::Base` when loading `ActiveJob::TestHelper`.

    *Maxime Réty*

*   Preserve the serialized timezone when deserializing `ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone` arguments.

    *Joshua Young*

*   Fix ActiveJob arguments serialization to correctly serialize String subclasses having custom serializers.

    *fatkodima*


## Rails 7.1.0.rc1 (September 27, 2023) ##

*   Set `scheduled_at` attribute as a Time object instead of epoch seconds, and serialize and deserialize the value
    when enqueued. Assigning a numeric/epoch value to scheduled_at= is deprecated; use a Time object instead.

    Deserializes `enqueued_at` as a Time instead of ISO8601 String.

    *Ben Sheldon*

*   Clarify the backoff strategy for the recommended `:wait` option when retrying jobs

    `wait: :exponentially_longer` is waiting polynomially longer, so it is now recommended to use `wait: :polynomially_longer` to keep the same behavior.

    *Victor Mours*


## Rails 7.1.0.beta1 (September 13, 2023) ##

*   Fix Active Job log message to correctly report a job failed to enqueue
    when the adapter raises an `ActiveJob::EnqueueError`.

    *Ben Sheldon*

*   Add `after_discard` method.

    This method lets job authors define a block which will be run when a job is about to be discarded. For example:

    ```ruby
    class AfterDiscardJob < ActiveJob::Base
*   Don't double log the `job` when using `ActiveRecord::QueryLog`

    Previously if you set `config.active_record.query_log_tags` to an array that included
    `:job`, the job name would get logged twice. This bug has been fixed.

    *Alex Ghiculescu*

*   Add support for Sidekiq's transaction-aware client

    *Jonathan del Strother*

*   Remove QueAdapter from Active Job.

    After maintaining Active Job QueAdapter by Rails and Que side
    to support Ruby 3 keyword arguments and options provided as top level keywords,
    it is quite difficult to maintain it this way.

    Active Job Que adapter can be included in the future version of que gem itself.

    *Yasuo Honda*

*   Fix BigDecimal (de)serialization for adapters using JSON.

    Previously, BigDecimal was listed as not needing a serializer.  However,
    when used with an adapter storing the job arguments as JSON, it would get
    serialized as a simple String, resulting in deserialization also producing
    a String (instead of a BigDecimal).

    By using a serializer, we ensure the round trip is safe.

    To ensure applications using BigDecimal job arguments are not subject to
    race conditions during deployment (where a replica running a version of
    Rails without BigDecimalSerializer fails to deserialize an argument
    serialized with it), `ActiveJob.use_big_decimal_serializer` is disabled by
    default, and can be set to true in a following deployment..

    *Sam Bostock*

*   Preserve full-precision `enqueued_at` timestamps for serialized jobs,
    allowing more accurate reporting of how long a job spent waiting in the
    queue before it was performed.
    - `active_job.step`

    *Adrianna Chang*

*   Deprecate built-in `sidekiq` adapter.

    If you're using this adapter, upgrade to `sidekiq` 7.3.3 or later to use the `sidekiq` gem's adapter.

    *fatkodima*

*   Remove deprecated internal `SuckerPunch` adapter in favor of the adapter included with the `sucker_punch` gem.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove support to set `ActiveJob::Base.enqueue_after_transaction_commit` to `:never`, `:always` and `:default`.

require "active_support/core_ext/object/try"
require "action_view/helpers/tags/placeholderable"

module ActionText
  module TagHelper
    cattr_accessor(:id, instance_accessor: false) { 0 }

    def rich_textarea_tag(name, value = nil, options = {}, &block)
      value = capture(&block) if value.nil? && block_given?
      options = options.symbolize_keys
      form = options.delete(:form)

      options[:input] ||= "trix_input_#{ActionText::TagHelper.id += 1}"
      options[:class] ||= "trix-content"

      options[:data] ||= {}
      options[:data][:direct_upload_url] ||= main_app.rails_direct_uploads_url
      options[:data][:blob_url_template] ||= main_app.rails_service_blob_url(":signed_id", ":filename")

      editor_tag = content_tag("trix-editor", "", options)
      input_tag = hidden_field_tag(name, value.try(:to_trix_html) || value, id: options[:input], form: form)

      input_tag + editor_tag
    end
    alias_method :rich_text_area_tag, :rich_textarea_tag
  end
end

module ActionView::Helpers
  class Tags::ActionText < Tags::Base
    include Tags::Placeholderable

    delegate :dom_id, to: ActionView::RecordIdentifier

    def render(&block)
      options = @options.stringify_keys
      add_default_name_and_field(options)
      options["input"] ||= dom_id(object, [options["id"], :trix_input].compact.join("_")) if object
      html_tag = @template_object.rich_textarea_tag(options.delete("name"), options.fetch("value") { value }, options.except("value"), &block)
      error_wrapping(html_tag)
    end
  end

content.content:
*   Direct upload progress accounts for server processing time.

    *Jeremy Daer*

*   Delegate `ActiveStorage::Filename#to_str` to `#to_s`

    Supports checking String equality:

    ```ruby
    filename = ActiveStorage::Filename.new("file.txt")
    filename == "file.txt" # => true
    filename in "file.txt" # => true
    "file.txt" == filename # => true
    ```

    *Sean Doyle*

*   A Blob will no longer autosave associated Attachment.

    This fixes an issue where a record with an attachment would have
    its dirty attributes reset, preventing your `after commit` callbacks
    on that record to behave as expected.

    Note that this change doesn't require any changes on your application
    and is supposed to be internal. Active Storage Attachment will continue

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "sidekiq/job"

module Sidekiq
  class Rails < ::Rails::Engine
    class Reloader
      def initialize(app = ::Rails.application)
        @app = app
      end

      def call
        @app.reloader.wrap do
          yield
        end
      end

      def inspect
        "#<Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader @app=#{@app.class.name}>"
      end
    end

    # By including the Options module, we allow AJs to directly control sidekiq features
    # via the *sidekiq_options* class method and, for instance, not use AJ's retry system.
    # AJ retries don't show up in the Sidekiq UI Retries tab, save any error data, can't be
    # manually retried, don't automatically die, etc.
    #
    #   class SomeJob < ActiveJob::Base
    #     queue_as :default
    #     sidekiq_options retry: 3, backtrace: 10
    #     def perform
    #     end
    #   end
    initializer "sidekiq.active_job_integration" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        include ::Sidekiq::Job::Options unless respond_to?(:sidekiq_options)
      end
    end

    config.before_configuration do
      dep = ActiveSupport::Deprecation.new("7.0", "Sidekiq")
      dep.deprecate_methods(Sidekiq.singleton_class,
        default_worker_options: :default_job_options,
        "default_worker_options=": :default_job_options=)
    end

    # This hook happens after all initializers are run, just before returning
    # from config/environment.rb back to sidekiq/cli.rb.
    #
    # None of this matters on the client-side, only within the Sidekiq process itself.
    config.after_initialize do
      Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
        config[:reloader] = Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader.new

        # This is the integration code necessary so that if a job uses `Rails.logger.info "Hello"`,
        # it will appear in the Sidekiq console with all of the job context.
        unless ::Rails.logger == config.logger || ::ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?(::Rails.logger, $stdout)
          if ::Rails::VERSION::STRING < "7.1"
            ::Rails.logger.extend(::ActiveSupport::Logger.broadcast(config.logger))
          else
            ::Rails.logger.broadcast_to(config.logger)
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

## Rails 8.1.0 (October 22, 2025) ## * De-couple `@rails/actiontext/attachment_upload.js` from `Trix.Attachment` Implement `@rails/actiontext/index.js` with a `direct-upload:progress` event listeners and `Promise` resolution. *Sean Doyle* * Capture block content for form helper methods ```erb <%= rich_textarea_tag :content, nil do %>

hello world

<% end %> <%= rich_textarea :message, :content, input: "trix_input_1" do %>

hello world

<% end %> <%= form_with model: Message.new do |form| %> <%= form.rich_textarea :content do %>

hello world

<% end %> <% end %> ``` *Sean Doyle* * Generalize `:rich_text_area` Capybara selector Prepare for more Action Text-capable WYSIWYG editors by making `:rich_text_area` rely on the presence of `[role="textbox"]` and `[contenteditable]` HTML attributes rather than a `` element. *Sean Doyle* * Forward `fill_in_rich_text_area` options to Capybara ```ruby fill_in_rich_textarea "Rich text editor", id: "trix_editor_1", with: "Hello world!" ``` *Sean Doyle* * Attachment upload progress accounts for server processing time. *Jeremy Daer* * The Trix dependency is now satisfied by a gem, `action_text-trix`, rather than vendored files. This allows applications to bump Trix versions independently of Rails releases. Effectively this also upgrades Trix to `>= 2.1.15`. *Mike Dalessio* * Change `ActionText::RichText#embeds` assignment from `before_save` to `before_validation` *Sean Doyle* Please check [8-0-stable](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-0-stable/actiontext/CHANGELOG.md) for previous changes.

# By default returns <tt>"async"</tt>.
      def queue_adapter_name
        self.queue_adapter = :async if _queue_adapter_name.nil?
        _queue_adapter_name
      end

      # Specify the backend queue provider. The default queue adapter
      # is the +:async+ queue. See QueueAdapters for more
      # information.
      def queue_adapter=(name_or_adapter)
        case name_or_adapter
        when Symbol, String
          queue_adapter = ActiveJob::QueueAdapters.lookup(name_or_adapter).new
          queue_adapter.try(:check_adapter)
          assign_adapter(name_or_adapter.to_s, queue_adapter)
        else
          if queue_adapter?(name_or_adapter)
            adapter_name = ActiveJob.adapter_name(name_or_adapter).underscore
            assign_adapter(adapter_name, name_or_adapter)
          else
            raise ArgumentError
          end
        end

982:*   Remove deprecated support to passing coder and class as second argument to `serialize`.
1064:    used by the default serializer.
1234:    Previously, the encryptor instance only allowed an encrypted value serialized as a `String` to be passed to the message serializer.
1236:    Now, the encryptor lets the configured `message_serializer` decide which types of serialized encrypted values are supported. A custom serialiser is therefore allowed to serialize `ActiveRecord::Encryption::Message` objects using a type other than `String`.
1366:*   Fix `where(field: values)` queries when `field` is a serialized attribute
1367:    (for example, when `field` uses `ActiveRecord::Base.serialize` or is a JSON
*   `ActiveRecord::Base.serialize` signature changed.

    Rather than a single positional argument that accepts two possible
    types of values, `serialize` now accepts two distinct keyword arguments.

    Before:

    ```ruby
    serialize :content, JSON
    serialize :backtrace, Array
    ```

    After:

    ```ruby
    serialize :content, coder: JSON
    serialize :backtrace, type: Array
    ```

    *Jean Boussier*

# Risk report: upgrading Rails 7.0.8.7 to 8.1.0 in Margin Notes

The biggest risks are changes that don't raise errors. Four of them change saved data or what readers see, and one breaks running jobs while old and new versions run side by side during a deploy. The existing tests would catch most of these, but the report shows where to look. Most of the remaining changes raise an error that booting the app or running the test suite would catch.

I worked only from the two released gem versions (downloaded to `/tmp/railsdiff/src/`), the 7.1, 7.2 and 8.0 stable-branch changelogs (in `/tmp/railsdiff/changelogs/`), and the app's code. I didn't install, run, or change anything. Changelog line anchors are for the stable branches as of today and may drift.

Each claim is labelled: **[changelog]**, **[code]** (I read it in the gem source), or **[inference]**.

## Facts about the app that the ratings depend on (please correct any that are wrong)

1. **Database:** PostgreSQL only, through pg 1.6.0 (`config/database.yml`). There is no MySQL or SQLite.
2. **Background jobs:** Active Job uses Rails' built-in `:sidekiq` adapter with Sidekiq 6.5.12 and redis 4.8.1 (`config/application.rb:24`). Tests use the `:test` adapter. `ExportJob` is a native Sidekiq job.
3. **Job arguments that matter:**
   - `DigestJob` receives a time in the reader's own time zone and a `BigDecimal` (`app/models/user.rb:35,41`).
   - `NoteReminderJob` is scheduled with an Integer epoch (`app/models/note.rb:61`).
   - `CitationEnrichmentJob` uses `retry_on wait: :exponentially_longer`.
4. **I assumed the deploy is rolling,** so web servers and Sidekiq workers will briefly run different Rails versions. Please confirm.
5. **Output:** the app renders HTML only (ERB, Sprockets, importmap, Turbo). Jbuilder is installed but there are no JSON endpoints.
6. **Rich text:** Action Text, with a vendored Trix 1.3.5 loaded as a classic script (`app/views/layouts/application.html.erb:13`). The sanitizer allowlist is customised in `config/initializers/action_text.rb:3`.
7. **Files:** Active Storage on the local Disk service.
8. **Caching:** production doesn't set `cache_store`, so Rails' default file store applies [inference]. The only cache use is the fragment cache in `app/views/exports/_export.html.erb:26`.
9. **Framework defaults:** I assumed `config.load_defaults 7.0` stays in place. Several 7.1–8.1 defaults would break this app if adopted; they're listed at the end.
10. **Settings:** the citation provider's settings come from `Rails.application.secrets` / `config/secrets.yml`.
11. **Time zones:** each reader has a stored zone name, and the app's own zone is UTC.
12. **Tests:** the test environment sets `config.action_dispatch.show_exceptions = false` (`config/environments/test.rb:31`).

## High risk

### H1. `return` inside a transaction now commits instead of rolling back
- **Before:** in 7.0, leaving a `transaction` block early with `return` rolled the transaction back [code].
- **Now:** 7.1 added a setting to commit instead, and 7.2 removed the old behavior, so 8.1 always commits [code, changelog].
- **Where:** `Import#apply` (`app/models/import.rb:53-58`) does `return false unless row.note.save` inside `transaction`.
- **What could go wrong:** when a later row fails, the `Import` and every earlier note stay saved. The controller still renders "Nothing has been saved", and `ARCHITECTURE.md` promises all-or-nothing imports.
- **Tests:** `test/controllers/imports_controller_test.rb:65` should catch it.
- **Links:** [AR 7.1 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L864), [AR 7.2 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L932), [PR #48600](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/48600).

### H2. `record[:id]` no longer returns a custom primary key
- **Before:** `read_attribute(:id)` mapped `"id"` to the primary key [code].
- **Now:** 8.1 reads a literal `id` attribute. `citations` has no `id` column, so the call returns `nil` without raising [code: `AttributeSet#[]` falls back to `Attribute::Null`].
- **Where:** `Import#receipt` uses `citation && citation[:id]` (`app/models/import.rb:68`).
- **What could go wrong:** the DOI column of every downloaded receipt CSV becomes blank. The fix is `citation.id` or `citation.doi`.
- **Tests:** `imports_controller_test.rb:45` should catch it.
- **Links:** [AR 7.1 deprecation](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L779), [AR 7.2 removal](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L986), [PR #49019](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/49019).

### H3. `HashWithIndifferentAccess#stringify_keys` now converts Integer keys
- **Before:** in 7.0, `stringify_keys` was just `dup`, so Integer keys stayed Integers [code].
- **Now:** in 8.0+, every key becomes a String [changelog, code].
- **Where:** `Import#annotations` builds a hash keyed by Integer line numbers (`app/models/import.rb:38-42`). `app/views/imports/preview.html.erb:22` calls `.stringify_keys`, then line 42 looks up `annotations[row.line]` with an Integer.
- **What could go wrong:** every annotation silently disappears from the import preview.
- **Tests:** `imports_controller_test.rb:22` should catch it.
- **Links:** [AS 8.0 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-0-stable/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L366), [PR #53125](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53125).

### H4. Time arguments to jobs now keep their time zone
- **Before:** in 7.0, the worker rebuilt the time in `Time.zone`, which is UTC [code].
- **Now:** 8.1 stores the zone name with the time and restores it, so the time arrives in the reader's zone [code].
- **Where:**
  - `User#request_digest` passes `Time.current.in_time_zone(time_zone)` (`app/models/user.rb:35,41`).
  - `DigestMailer#daily_digest` uses `requested_at.to_date` and `requested_at.all_day` (`app/mailers/digest_mailer.rb:8-9`).
- **What could go wrong:**
  - Digests switch from the UTC day to the reader's local day: a different subject date and a different set of notes. The Redis reservation still uses the UTC day.
  - The code comments and `ARCHITECTURE.md` describe the old behavior.
  - A 7.0-queued job run by an 8.1 worker keeps the old UTC behavior [code: falls back to `Time.zone`].
- **Tests:** `test/controllers/digests_controller_test.rb:33-35` should catch it.
- **Links:** [AJ 7.1 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L64), [PR #50240](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/50240).

### H5. `BigDecimal` job arguments now use a serializer that 7.0 workers can't read
- **Before:** in 7.0, a `BigDecimal` went into Sidekiq's JSON as a plain string.
- **Now:** 8.1 always wraps it as `{"_aj_serialized" => "ActiveJob::Serializers::BigDecimalSerializer", ...}`. 7.1 kept this behind a setting for safe rollouts, and 8.0 removed the setting [code, changelog].
- **Where:** `DigestJob.perform_later(self, requested_at, reading_completion)` (`app/models/user.rb:41`).
- **What could go wrong:**
  - While both versions run, a 7.0 worker can't find that serializer class. The job fails to deserialize and Sidekiq retries it until an 8.1 worker picks it up.
  - The reader's Redis reservation is already taken, so they can't ask again that day.
  - Upgrade workers before web servers, or drain the queue first. The mailer's `BigDecimal(params[:completion])` works with either form.
- **Links:** [AJ 7.1 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L226), [AJ 8.0 removal](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-0-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L69), [PR #45618](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/45618).

### H6. `TimeWithZone#to_time` now keeps the zone, not the UTC offset
- **Before:** with 7.0 defaults, `to_time` kept only the UTC offset [code].
- **Now:** 8.1 always returns `getlocal(time_zone)`, and the setting is deprecated and ignored [code, changelog].
- **Where:** `Note#next_day_reminder_at` is `reminder_at.to_time + 86_400` (`app/models/note.rb:43-45`). It is shown in `app/views/notes/_reminder.html.erb:19`.
- **What could go wrong:**
  - Across a daylight-saving change, the "24 hours later" preview now shows the new offset, e.g. 08:00 −05:00 instead of 09:00 −04:00.
  - The stored epoch is unchanged. Only what readers see changes, and the code comment and `ARCHITECTURE.md` become wrong.
- **Tests:** `test/controllers/reminders_controller_test.rb:21` asserts the old output.
- **Links:** [AS 8.0 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-0-stable/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L460), [AS 8.1 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v8.1.0/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L20).

### H7. The "Astana" time zone now points at a different TZInfo zone
- **Before:** the 7.0 `TimeZone::MAPPING` mapped "Astana" to Asia/Dhaka [code].
- **Now:** in 8.1 it maps to Asia/Almaty. "Asuncion" was added, "Greenland" maps to America/Nuuk, and "Canberra" maps to Australia/Canberra [code]. The last two are aliases of the old zones [inference].
- **Where:** stored `users.time_zone`, validated at `app/models/user.rb:13` and used at `app/models/user.rb:22` and `app/models/note.rb:37`.
- **What could go wrong:** current tzdata has Almaty at UTC+5, while Dhaka is UTC+6 [inference]. Readers who picked "Astana" would see reminder times, and parse the times they enter, an hour differently. Check how many users have that zone.
- **Links:** [AS 7.2 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L348), [PR #51317](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/51317).

## Medium risk

### M1. `Rails.application.secrets` was removed in 7.2
- **Where:** `Citation::Provider#initialize` (`app/models/citation/provider.rb:13`), `config/secrets.yml`, and `test/controllers/citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:45,117-122`, which also assigns to `secrets` at runtime.
- **What breaks:** a `NoMethodError` on the first lookup. Booting doesn't catch it, because the call is only made when a provider is built.
- **Decision needed:** where the settings live: credentials, `config_for`, or `ENV`. Whatever replaces `secrets.yml` must keep the `.to_json` quoting so values like `"00123"` stay strings. The test at line 40 covers this.
- **Links:** [Railties 7.1](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/railties/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L298), [Railties 7.2](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/railties/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L148). [changelog, code]

### M2. Rails' built-in Sidekiq adapter is deprecated in 8.1 and goes away in 8.2
- **Where:** `config/application.rb:24`. The adapter still works in 8.1 and logs a deprecation warning when it is configured at boot [code].
- **Decision needed:** the replacement is Sidekiq 7.3.3 or later, which ships its own adapter. Sidekiq 7 uses `redis-client` instead of the `redis` gem [inference], which affects two places:
  - `Sidekiq.redis { |r| r.sadd(key, id) }` would return an Integer, and `0` is truthy in Ruby, which would break the once-a-day digest check (`app/models/user.rb:38`).
  - `rescue Redis::BaseError` (`app/models/notebook.rb:28`) and the tests that raise `Redis::CannotConnectError` would no longer match.
- **Link:** [AJ 8.1 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v8.1.0/activejob/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L19). [changelog, code]

### M3. Trix now comes from the `action_text-trix` gem (Trix 2.1.15 or later)
- **Where:**
  - The layout loads the vendored `trix-1.3.5.js` (`app/views/layouts/application.html.erb:10-13`).
  - `app/assets/stylesheets/actiontext.css:6` does `require trix`, which would now pull in Trix 2's CSS next to Trix 1's JavaScript.
  - `@rails/actiontext` is pinned to `actiontext.js` (`config/importmap.rb:8`). In 8.1 that file is a UMD bundle, where 7.0's was an ES module; 8.1 also ships `actiontext.esm.js` [code].
- **Decision needed:** keep Trix 1.3.5 or adopt Trix 2, which is an ES module. Trix 2 changes the editor's paste sanitising and the stored HTML [inference]. The details/summary flattening described in `ARCHITECTURE.md` needs re-checking either way.
- **Links:** [AT 8.1 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v8.1.0/actiontext/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L53), [AT 7.1 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/actiontext/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L78). [changelog, code]

### M4. `ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_tags` now defaults to nil
- **Where:** `config/initializers/action_text.rb:3` does `allowed_tags += %w[details summary]`. That becomes `nil + [...]`, a `NoMethodError` at boot [code].
- **Why medium:** the defaults are now computed in `sanitizer_allowed_tags`, an instance method you can't call on the module. The fix has to rebuild the list as `sanitizer.class.allowed_tags + [action-text-attachment, figure, figcaption]` plus your additions. A naive `allowed_tags = %w[details summary]` would silently remove most formatting and all attachments.
- **Link:** [AT 7.1 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/actiontext/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L117). [changelog, code]

### M5. `show_exceptions = false` now means "show all exceptions"
- **Where:** `config/environments/test.rb:31`. In 8.1, any value other than `:none` or `:rescuable` is treated as `:all` [code].
- **What breaks:** every `assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound)` around a request fails, because a 404 page is rendered instead. Tests that don't check status would also hide unexpected 500s.
- **Decision needed:** `:none` keeps today's behavior; `:rescuable` is the 7.1+ generator default.
- **Link:** [AP 7.2 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/actionpack/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L210). [changelog, code]

### M6. A negative cache `expires_in` is now handled differently
- **Where:** `app/views/exports/_export.html.erb:26` passes `expires_in: export.expires_at - Time.current`, which is negative once an export has expired.
- **Before:** 7.0 wrote an entry that was already expired [code].
- **Now:** with `load_defaults 7.0`, 8.1 drops the option, logs an `ArgumentError` at error level, reports it to `Rails.error`, and stores the fragment with no expiry [code]. The rendered "Expired" text stays correct, but every render of an expired export logs an error.
- **New default:** if you adopt `raise_on_invalid_cache_expiration_time` (a 7.1 default), the exports page raises instead.
- **Link:** [AS 7.1 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L1129). [code, changelog]

## Low risk (booting the app or running the tests would catch these)

- **`serialize :tags, JSON`** (`app/models/note.rb:12`) raises `ArgumentError` when the class loads. Use `coder: JSON`. The JSON written to the column is unchanged [code]. [AR 7.2](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L982)
- **`enum status: {...}, _prefix: true`** (`app/models/note.rb:10`) raises. Use `enum :status, {...}, prefix: true`. [AR 8.0](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-0-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L713)
- **`alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color`** (`app/models/note.rb:14`) raises `ArgumentError` when Note's attribute methods are first generated, because `color` is a store accessor, not an attribute. Use `alias_method` for both the reader and the writer. [AR 7.2](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L1051)
- **`where(notebooks: @notebook)`** (`app/controllers/notes_controller.rb:12`): a plural name for a singular association no longer resolves, so the query hits a nonexistent `notes.notebooks` column and PostgreSQL raises. Use `where(notebook: @notebook)`. [AR 7.2](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L994)
- **`fragments.sum`** on Strings (`app/models/export.rb:42`) raises `TypeError` in the worker. Use `join`. [AS 7.1](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L688)
- **`retry_on ..., wait: :exponentially_longer`** (`app/jobs/citation_enrichment_job.rb:7`) only raises when a retry happens, so booting won't catch it. The failure-recording block would then never run. Use `:polynomially_longer`; the delays are the same. `citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:60` catches it. [AJ 7.2](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L110)
- **`set(wait_until: reminder_epoch)` with an Integer** (`app/models/note.rb:61`) raises `NoMethodError` (`utc` on an Integer) when the job is serialized [code]. Use `Time.at(epoch)`. [AJ 7.2](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L114)
- **`get "/notes", "/journal", to: ...`** (`config/routes.rb:18`) raises `ArgumentError` when routes load. Split it into two `get` lines and keep `journal_path`. [AP 8.1](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v8.1.0/actionpack/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L107)
- **`form_with(model: nil, ...)`** (`app/views/notes/index.html.erb:12`) raises. Drop `model: nil`. [AV 8.0](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-0-stable/actionview/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L193)
- **Action Text `to_plain_text`** now drops script and style contents and numbers ordered lists by element, which can slightly change export Markdown (`app/models/export.rb:78`) [code].
- **The development secret file** moves from `tmp/development_secret.txt` to `tmp/local_secret.txt`, so local sessions reset once [code].
- **`schema.rb` columns are now sorted alphabetically** (diff noise on the next dump), and parallel test databases use a `_N` suffix. [AR 8.1](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v8.1.0/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md?plain=1#L689)
- **Dependencies the upgrade moves or adds** are compatible with the current lockfile [code: gemspec metadata]:
  - New gems: `action_text-trix`, `rackup`, `rack-session`, `useragent`.
  - Ruby 3.3.6 and rack 2.2 are accepted, which Sidekiq 6.5 needs.
  - The concurrent-ruby 1.3.4 and minitest 5 pins still fit.
  - Sidekiq 6.5.12 already supports the Rails 7.1+ logger API.

## Defaults that stay off while `load_defaults 7.0` is kept, but would break this app if adopted [code]

- **`raise_on_assign_to_attr_readonly`:** the notebook settings form resubmits the read-only `slug` (`app/controllers/notebooks_controller.rb:40`, `app/models/notebook.rb:8`).
- **`default_column_serializer = nil`:** `serialize :preferences` has no coder (`app/models/notebook.rb:7`).
- **`postgresql_adapter_decode_dates`:** `Date.iso8601` would be handed a `Date` and raise `TypeError` (`app/models/notebook.rb:40`).
- **`raise_on_invalid_cache_expiration_time`:** see M6.
- **`strict_freshness`:** changes `stale?` in `app/controllers/export_downloads_controller.rb:11`.
- **HTML5 `sanitizer_vendor`:** changes Action Text rendering.
- **`message_serializer` and `cache_format_version` 7.1:** these change cookie and cache formats, which is a problem while old and new versions run side by side.

## Parts of Rails I judged not relevant

- MySQL, SQLite and Trilogy adapter changes: the app uses PostgreSQL.
- Solid Queue, Solid Cache and Solid Cable: not used.
- Propshaft, Kamal and the new generator or authentication templates: they only affect new apps.
- Action Mailbox: not used.
- Active Storage variants, previews, S3, GCS and Azure: only the Disk service is used, with no image processor.
- Action Cable: only the empty base classes exist, and the production Redis adapter accepts redis 4.8.
- Composite primary keys, encryption, multiple databases and sharding: not used.
- `params.expect`: optional; `require.permit` still works.
- JSON-response changes such as `escape_json_responses`: the app has no JSON endpoints.
- `has_secure_password`'s 72-byte limit: the app has no password-setting form.
- `enqueue_after_transaction_commit`: it defaults to false in 8.1, so `with_lock` plus `perform_later` behaves as it does today [code].

One suggestion: upgrade in steps (7.1, then 7.2, 8.0 and 8.1) with the test suite running at each step. Many of the items above are deprecation warnings in an intermediate version, and jumping straight to 8.1 skips those warnings. `ARCHITECTURE.md` describes H1, H4 and H6 in their current form and will need updating.
